<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="DjR" /></noinclude><section begin="par114" />''est'', unless we simply read {{GHGheb|text=יִמְצָא}} with the LXX)<ref>P. Haupt ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|SBOT.|Sacred Books of the Old Testament, ed. by P. Haupt. Lpz. and Baltimore, 1893 ff.}}}}, Proverbs, p. 52, lines 10 ff.; ''Critical Notes on Esther'', p. 170, on 7:8) considers it possible that here and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=2|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=6|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=7|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=16|verse=30|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, as well as in 14:35, 17:21 before a noun, the {{GHGheb|text=ל}} is a survival of the emphatic {{GHGheb|text=ל}} with an ''imperf.'', which is especially common in Arabic. In that case {{GHGheb|text=לִמְצֹא}} must be read {{GHGheb|text=לִמְצָא}}, i.e. {{GHGheb|text=ל}} + {{GHGheb|text=יִמְצָא}}. But all the above instances can be taken as infinitives with {{GHGheb|text=ל}} without difficulty.</ref>; 20:25, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=3|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר לִֽהְיוֹת|translate=quod futurum est}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=11|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=12|verse=12|hidebook=1}} (in a negative statement); in a question, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=7|verse=8}} (''will he even''... ?). Cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=19}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|114|k}}
Of (''b'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי הַשַּׁ֫עַר לִסְגּוֹר|translate=and the gate was to be shut}} (had to be shut); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=109|verse=13}}.<ref>Somewhat different are the cases where {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה לְ}} with the infinitive (which is then used exactly as a substantive) implies ''to become something'', i.e. to meet with a particular fate, as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=24|verse=22}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=13|hidebook=1}}) {{GHGheb|text=לְבָעֵר|translate=for wasting}}, for which elsewhere frequently {{GHGheb|text=לְשַׁמָּה}} and the like; probably also {{GHGheb|text=לְבַלּוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=49|verse=15}} is to be explained in this way, the {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה}} being omitted.</ref> Mostly with the omission of {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=4|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=מֶה לַֽעֲשׂוֹת לָךְ וג׳|translate=what is to be done for thee?}} ({{GHGheb|text=הֲיֵשׁ לְדַבֶּר־לָךְ}}) ''wouldest thou be'' (lit. is it to be) ''spoken for to the king'', &c.? {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=13|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=לְהַכּוֹת|translate=it was to smite}} equivalent to ''thou shouldest have smitten''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=32|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=19|hidebook=1}} (?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=6}} (''habitandum est iis''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=9|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=10|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=22|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=8|verse=13}} (?), 11:22, 19:2, 36:19 (?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=9|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=1|verse=17}}. In a question {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=19|verse=2}}; after {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=5|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=15|verse=2|hidebook=1}}; after {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=23|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=5|verse=11}} and frequently.

{{GHGmargin-letter|114|l}}
Of the same kind also are the cases, in which the infinitive with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} depends on the idea of an obligation or permission (or prohibition); especially in such forms of expression as {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=עָלַי לָ֫תֶת לְךָ וג׳}} it was ''upon me'', i.e. it would have been ''my duty to give thee'', &c.<ref>{{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=4|verse=10}} (''cui dandum erat mihi'') appears to be similar; it may, however, be better, with Wellhausen, to omit the {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}}.</ref>; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=3|verse=1}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=13|verse=5}}) ''it is not for you to'' (i.e. are ye not bound to)?<ref>But in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=23|verse=20}} after {{GHGheb|text=וְלָ֫נוּ|translate=and our part shall be}} the infinitive without {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} stands as the subject of the sentence.</ref> with a negative, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=26|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹא לְךָ וג׳|translate=it pertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto the Lord, but}} only ''to the priests''; also {{GHGheb|text=אֵין לְ}} with an infinitive expresses ''it is not permitted'' (nefas est), ''may not'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=4|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=כִּי אֵין לָבוֹא|translate=for none might enter}}; 8:8, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=15|verse=2}};<ref>Quite different of course are such cases as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=וְכֹחַ אַ֫יִן לְלֵדָה|translate=and there is not strength to bring forth}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=20|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=4|verse=4}}.</ref> {{GHGheb|text=אֵין לְ}} with an infinitive is used in a somewhat different sense, equivalent to ''it is not feasible, not possible'', e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=40|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=3|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=5|verse=11}}.<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=אִשׁ}} (= {{GHGheb|text=יֵשׁ|translate=it is, there is}}) is used in a similar sense after {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}, the negative particle of asseveration, ''of a truth it is not'' possible ''to turn to the right hand or to the left''.</ref>—With either meaning {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} can be used instead of {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹא לְהַזְכִּיר|translate=nefas est}}, ''to make mention'' of the name of the Lord: but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=1|verse=19}} ''for it was not possible to drive out'', &c., perhaps, however, the text originally stood as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=17|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹא יָֽכְלוּ לְה׳}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=15|verse=2}}.
